beats.say: Nine in the morning. Everyone opens a dashboard.
At the same time, analysts run heavy ad-hoc queries. They collide.
beats.label: The collision
beats.head: Dashboards and ad-hoc queries collide

beats.say: Organize capacity by what the business needs first.
beats.label: Station 5.3 · Organizing workloads
beats.head: What does the business need first?

check.prompt: A weekly report is not urgent. How should its query run?
check.why: A batch query waits for free resources, so it does not fight the dashboards.

beats.say: Think of a hospital. Emergencies go first.
An interactive query is the emergency. It runs as soon as possible.
beats.label: Interactive (the default)
beats.head: Interactive: runs now

beats.say: A batch query can wait. It starts when resources are free.
beats.label: Batch priority
beats.head: Batch: waits its turn

beats.say: So send non-urgent reports as batch. They stop fighting the dashboards.
beats.label: Use it
beats.head: Non-urgent report? Make it batch.

beats.say: Give each kind of work its own reservation: dashboards, pipelines, ad-hoc.
beats.label: Reservations
beats.head: One reservation per kind of work

beats.say: Set a baseline on the important ones. Autoscaling covers the bursts.
beats.label: Baseline and autoscale
beats.head: Baseline for sure. Autoscale for bursts.

beats.say: And keep dev and test away from prod. An experiment must not starve production.
beats.label: Separate
beats.head: Dev must not starve prod

beats.say: To size it, watch slot use in the admin charts.
beats.label: How big?
beats.head: Watch slot use, then size

beats.say: Interactive runs now. Batch waits. Reservations and baselines decide who goes first.
beats.label: Station 5.3
